clue.text: Get rid of fine example that's a banger

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them, get rid of them
a cracker is informal for an excellent specimen

explanation.surface: Someone disposes of a superb specimen of a sausage, or perhaps of a noisy firework.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang both for a sausage and for a loud firework; here it is the firework.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is a small explosive firework, the kind that goes off with a loud crack.

clue.text: Attacker moving ahead

definitions.meaning: a striker, an attacking player in football or hockey

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the striker in a team and an adjective for heading towards the front.

clue.text: Religious person, bishop, in island pub, upset

indicators.note: the bishop letter goes in the middle of the island and pub pieces
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a bar is a pub
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric and a bishop are in an island pub, distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns I and BAR round to RABI, and 'in' puts B inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher and leader.

clue.text: Chant from choir, originally in Latin, modified in church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: the Latin letters, with the choir letter, are modified, rearranged
originally means only the first letter of choir is used

explanation.surface: A sung piece by a church choir, first in Latin and later adapted.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; it is 'in church' that does the inserting, after 'modified' has rearranged the choir's first letter with LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A canticle is a hymn or chant with words taken from the Bible, sung in services.

clue.text: Make amends an hour after midnight?

definitions.meaning: make up for a wrong, expiate
read as two words, the phrase gives the time 1 am

explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make up for a sin; split as two words it is the time 1 am.

clue.text: Dropped off cases and returned book

indicators.note: the sleep word encases, holds, the other piece

parts.note: kipped means slept, dropped off to sleep

indicators.note: the word and is returned, read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone fell asleep over their luggage and then took a book back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropped off' looks like delivered, but here it means fell asleep; 'cases' is a verb, holding the turned-round 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson's 1886 adventure novel bears this title.

clue.text: Bawdy drunken laird holding back, at first

indicators.note: the rearranged laird letters hold the other letter inside
drunken suggests the letters of laird are staggering about
at first means only the first letter of back is used

explanation.surface: A crude, tipsy Scottish landowner is restrained at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landowner. 'drunken' rearranges LAIRD to RIALD, which holds B.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald and bawdy both describe coarse, rude humour.

clue.text: Breakfast dish in Périgord, unusually

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of the place name are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd morning meal eaten in the Périgord region of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Oats boiled with water or milk make a hot morning cereal.

clue.text: Watching international show?

parts.note: watching a game means being at it
a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: Someone at an international match wonders whether it counts as a show.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket game, so 'watching international' is being at the Test.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to show or bear witness that something is true.

clue.text: Pantomime character cross about old boy in hospital

indicators.note: the cross word goes about, surrounding, the other pieces

parts.note: a rood is a crucifix, a cross
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
H is the abbreviation for hospital on road signs and maps

explanation.surface: A pantomime actor is angry with a former pupil lying in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is a British Christmas stage show; the outlaw of Sherwood Forest is a stock figure in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw of Sherwood is a regular hero of British Christmas pantomimes.

clue.text: Swell coming from vessel circling lake

indicators.note: the vessel goes round, circling, the lake letter

parts.note: a boat is a vessel
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A wave rises from a ship going round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell and to bloat both mean to puff up or distend.

clue.text: Stupid lapse at work in A&E

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in, between, the two letters of A&E

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, contributes its letters A and E
a sin is a moral lapse
in means at work, as in 'he's in today'

explanation.surface: A foolish slip-up by staff on duty in the hospital emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the British name for a hospital's emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine, literally donkey-like, means foolish or silly.

clue.text: Free, generally

definitions.meaning: on the loose, escaped and not captured
as a whole, as in 'the public in general'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both roaming free and in general, as in 'society as a whole'.

clue.text: Work required on old jacket? Thrower may need it for the game

definitions.text: Thrower may need it for the game

indicators.note: the work piece is needed after, tacked on to, the jacket

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket of Renaissance times
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: An antique jacket needs mending; meanwhile a player needs something to win the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts the 'thrower' must often finish on a double; double twenty, at the top of the board, is a favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Double twenty, the segment at the top of a dartboard, is a common finishing target for a darts player.

clue.text: Rap suits comic mentally

indicators.note: a comic version of the words is a jumbled one

explanation.surface: Rap music fits a comedian's frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstairs' is informal for in the head, as in 'not much upstairs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, upstairs means in the head, so in terms of intelligence or the mind.

clue.text: Programme I came across in list

indicators.note: the I and met pieces are put in the list word

parts.note: a table is a list of data
met means came across, encountered

explanation.surface: A TV show the speaker found in the listings.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of events and their times is a programme in the sense of a plan.

clue.text: Ready for publication? Some expedition wanted

indicators.note: only some of the word expedition is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A writer asks whether an expedition account is ready to print, wanting part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To ready text for publication is to correct and revise it, the job of an editor.

clue.text: Vociferous, head of sub-committee over ballistic missile

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece
head of means just the first letter of sub-committee

parts.note: Trident is a submarine-launched ballistic missile

explanation.surface: A loud chairman of a sub-committee discusses a nuclear weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Strident and vociferous both mean loud and insistent.

clue.text: Done in since halving physical training?

indicators.note: the PT letters are split into halves by the word put between them

parts.note: as means since, as in 'as it rained, we stayed in'

explanation.surface: Someone is exhausted because their gym sessions were cut in half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done in' suggests exhausted, but 'Done' alone is the definition and 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done is over, finished, gone by.

clue.text: Fertiliser in jardinière perhaps has worked

parts.note: a jardinière is an ornamental plant pot, an example of a pot

indicators.note: worked means the letters of has are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Plant feed in a decorative flowerpot has done its job.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash, a potassium compound, is a common garden fertiliser.

clue.text: Knight quits Mastermind, unexpectedly, halfway through

indicators.note: the remaining letters fall out in an unexpected order
the knight letter leaves, quits, the word Mastermind

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knighted contestant walks out of the TV quiz Mastermind halfway through filming.
explanation.walkthrough: Mastermind is a long-running British TV quiz show. Removing N from MASTERMIND leaves MASTERMID, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In midstream means in the middle of an activity, partway through.

clue.text: You'll be mad if you lose them in a game

definitions.text: You'll be mad if you lose them
definitions.meaning: to lose one's ... is an idiom for going mad
a children's game of rolling glass balls

explanation.definitionFit: Losing your marbles is slang for going mad, and marbles is also a children's game.

clue.text: Out when shelter promised initially

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
lee is shelter from the wind

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of promised is used

explanation.surface: Someone is away when the shelter that was promised first arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Out, as in out cold, means unconscious or sleeping.

clue.text: Passage in broadcast Mike overlooked

indicators.note: the M is overlooked, left out of the broadcast word

parts.note: to transmit is to broadcast
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A section of a radio show in which a presenter called Mike was ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage from one place to another, as in goods in transit.

clue.text: Spectacularly good performance in tie involving student, I hesitate to say

indicators.note: the tie word involves, wraps around, the student letter

parts.note: to bind is to tie
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
er is the sound one makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: A dazzling showing in a cup match that features a student; the speaker is reluctant to admit it.
explanation.walkthrough: A blinder is British informal for an outstanding display, especially in sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a blinder is British slang for giving an outstanding display in a game.

clue.text: Yellowish-brown insect biting one on end of leg

indicators.note: the insect word bites, closes round, the other letters

parts.note: a bee is an insect
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: end of means only the last letter of leg is used

explanation.surface: A tawny bug stings someone on the bottom of their leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Beige is a pale sandy fawn colour.

clue.text: Gloomy doctor on organ

indicators.note: in a down clue the doctor piece sits on top of the organ piece

parts.note: the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A doctor looks miserable examining a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, meaning dismal.

clue.text: Minister to deal

definitions.meaning: attend to the needs of, look after someone
hand out, as in dealing or dishing out food

explanation.definitionFit: To serve is both to wait on or tend to people and to dish out portions or a ball.

clue.text: Spouse quite possibly in prison

parts.note: a bride is a newly married spouse
well means quite possibly, as in 'it may well rain'

explanation.surface: A husband or wife may well be behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name became a general word for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, after a notorious old London house of correction, is a dated word for a jail.

clue.text: Here members salute

parts.note: present means here, as in answering a roll call
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Members of a group in attendance raise a salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Present arms is a military salute in which a rifle is held upright in front of the body.
